Sundial (Windows)
=================

A small sun on your desktop, showing the Claude Code sessions you have running
(what each is doing, how long it has been going, how much context is used) and
— if you have a Claude Max or Pro subscription — how much of your usage
allowance is left.

* An unofficial personal project. Not affiliated with Anthropic, and neither
  endorsed nor supported by them. The usage half relies on an undocumented
  endpoint and may stop working at any time.


First, the important part: you do not have to sign in
-----------------------------------------------------
The program has two halves, and they are independent:

· Session state and context consumption — read from local files on your own
  machine. No account, no subscription; it works as soon as you open it.

· The two usage dials — these need a Claude Max or Pro subscription. Without
  one, Claude's authorisation page states that connecting Claude Code requires
  Max or Pro, and refuses. That is expected, not a fault in the program.

So: with no subscription, skip step 3 below. The sun and the session blocks
work as normal; you simply will not have the two dials.

(The "or use an API key" option on that page does not help here. It is a
 separate billing arrangement, with no subscription-allowance figure to show.)


Getting started
---------------
1. Double-click Sundial.exe. There is no installer, and nothing is written
   into the system.
2. The first time you open it, Windows may show the blue "Windows protected
   your PC" dialogue. That is because the executable is not signed with a
   (paid) Microsoft code-signing certificate — it does not indicate a problem.
   Choose "More info" then "Run anyway".
3. Most people can skip this step. If your Claude Code is the command-line
   version and you have already signed in there, Sundial reuses the
   credentials it has stored: the two dials are simply there, with nothing
   for you to do.

   You only need to sign in yourself when that fails — most commonly because
   you use the Claude Code desktop app, which keeps its sign-in elsewhere —
   and you do have Max/Pro. In that case: double-click the sun, or right-click
   it and choose "sign in to Claude account". Your browser opens for you to
   sign in and approve, and you paste the code it gives you back into the app.
   Note that a code copied from an older authorisation tab will not work.
4. After that it just stays on your desktop. Hold and drag the sun to wherever
   you want it; hover to expand the detail, move away and it folds up again.


What it shows
-------------
When nothing is happening there is just a sun on your desktop — no card, no
backing. It takes up no room when it has nothing to say. Hover to expand.

· Below, one block per running Claude Code session: title, what it is doing,
  how long it has been running, how much context is used. A session waiting
  for you to choose something jumps to the top. Click a block to dismiss its
  "finished but unread" marker.
· With a subscription, a ring on either side of the sun:
  left (honey gold) is the five-hour allowance; right (apricot pink) is
  whichever weekly allowance is under the most pressure — the label may read
  "weekly" or the name of one particular model, whichever is tightest.
· The sun itself follows usage: a broad grin when there is room, a flat line
  around halfway, a frown and a reddened body as the limit approaches.
  It also reaches its rays towards whichever side is tightest, swaying back
  and forth, with the tips glowing in that side's colour and growing brighter
  the fuller it gets — so even folded down to a single sun, one glance tells
  you which side is under pressure.
· A grey sun with closed eyes and a few z's means no session is running.
  That is idle, not broken.

The percentage inside a session block is how much of the CONTEXT WINDOW is
used. When the bar turns deep red it is nearly full, and worth starting a
fresh session. That figure needs no subscription.


Controls
--------
Drag              move it (the position is remembered)
Double-click      starts sign-in if not signed in; otherwise refreshes now
Hover             expands the detail; moving away folds it up
Right-click       menu
Tray icon, left   brings the window to the front (without moving it)

Right-click menu:
  Sign in / sign in again to Claude account
  Sign out
  Refresh now
  Keep the usage breakdown open
  Open the web usage page
  Bring the pet back to the bottom-right     <- use this if it goes missing
  System blur background (experimental)
  Launch at login
  Quit Sundial


Notes and known limitations
---------------------------
· Requires Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit). The runtime is bundled; there is no
  need to install .NET separately.
· Only Claude Code installed NATIVELY on Windows is supported. If your Claude
  Code runs inside WSL, its transcripts live in the Linux subsystem's file
  system and this build cannot read them.
· The card is a hand-drawn translucent panel by default, not system blur.
  Windows acrylic applies only to a whole rectangular window, whereas this pet
  is a circle when folded and a rounded card when expanded — its shape changes
  every frame, so enabling acrylic exposes a rectangular backing outside the
  rounded corners. There is a "system blur background (experimental)" item in
  the right-click menu if you want to try it; it only has an effect on
  Windows 11. Either way, this aspect looks a notch behind the macOS build.
· The sign-in token is encrypted with Windows' own DPAPI and stored under
  %LOCALAPPDATA%\Sundial\, so only your account can read it.
· The window position and the menu toggles are kept in
  %APPDATA%\Sundial\shell.json, so they survive a restart.
· It reads the Claude Code transcripts under %USERPROFILE%\.claude, and
  specifically: record types, timestamps, busy/idle markers, token counts,
  session titles, and the opening characters of your messages — the last of
  these to recognise the "interrupted with Esc" and "background task finished"
  markers. So the text of your messages is read into memory in order to test
  its prefix. It is not displayed, not retained and not sent anywhere, but
  saying it "never touches your messages" would not be accurate, which is why
  it is spelt out here. Note also that session titles are shown on your
  desktop, so they are visible in screenshots and while screen-sharing.
· Apart from the one request that fetches usage (which only happens for
  subscribers), nothing is sent anywhere. No analytics, no crash reporting.
· While a session is running it uses CPU continuously (full-frame custom
  drawing plus periodic disk reads); with nothing running it drops to a low
  frame rate. The macOS build stops entirely when the display sleeps; this
  build does not yet manage that, which is a known gap.

To uninstall: delete Sundial.exe, then the %LOCALAPPDATA%\Sundial and
%APPDATA%\Sundial folders. If you enabled "launch at login", switch that off
in the right-click menu first.
